title: Fixed Slotted Tube and Low Trough Shaker Frame
description: One independently authored complete bamboo-style slotted-tube shaker frame in a fixed pose. A continuous low trough with two integral side walls and a finite flat sole carries two lower locating stems. Two separately authored stopped-bottom hollow tubes rise above it; each has a real deep inner cavity and a long side-open upper half-shell rather than a simple open circular pipe mouth. A full tall side-post and top-crosspiece frame, central upright and short fixed upper suspension ties hold the complete illustrated assembly. Each tube is one continuous closed material boundary from bottom disc through outer wall, variable-height open edge and complete inner wall; no painted opening. Unlike the bound panflute the main tubes are not tied into a mouth-aligned bank; unlike the suspended tubular-bell frame they have closed bottoms, deep longitudinal side openings and lower stems seated in a shared low trough, without a damper or pedal. All visible coordinates new, no old pipe or rack mesh extracted. Four opaque constant PBR roles, metres native Z up and horizontal full-bounds-centred ground datum. One static whole instrument-shaped prop zero scenes. Angklung-inspired exterior only, not a historically exact example: no acoustic tuning, sound, shaking clearance, suspension behaviour, playable mechanism, joint travel, material authenticity, load, fabrication or safety claim. No animation, rigging or interaction.
